I have nothing personal against Ms. Bilic, but this expert report should have been done by someone who is not involved in the war, and that person would have used the data available to the administration where Ms. Bilic works, the data from Serbia, from the government of the Serbian Krajina in exile, the Veritas NGO, and many other NGOs. That's what an unbiased expert would have done. We have an expert here who belongs, body and soul, to one of the warring sides, so her expertise cannot be comprehensive. It is partial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, there's something I don't understand, and maybe you could shed some light on this for me. This comparison that you would need and which you say should have been brought here or that we should have heard of, what is its purpose? How would you use it? What is the place that this comparison has in your own Defence case? Does this mean that according to you, the fact that there might have been thousands of Serbs who were killed in Croatia, would that justify killing thousands of Croats, maybe less than Serbs, but thousands of Croats? So how -- what is the role played by this comparison in your Defence case?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not a single crime can be justified, and especially not by prior crimes. But from an expert report of an objective expert, you would gain a true picture of that war. With this expert report, you get the impression that only Serbs killed, that only Serbs took prisoners of war, that only Serbs victimised civilians. This expert has no idea what happened throughout the territory of Croatia, because she says they were killed in one night lodgings versus camps, et cetera. They view it as justified capture or killing; but when one of ours kills or imprisons one of theirs, that is unjustified, that is a crime. What is important, I'm telling you, to understand is to understand the true nature of this war, where crimes were committed on both sides. I'm not justifying crimes on the Serbian side; but I don't want crimes on the Croatian side concealed. An unbiased expert report would give us objective data, so many people got killed, so many people passed through camps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to have to finish. I believe we'll finish tomorrow. Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say Mr. Seselj has had this document for a long time. If he had asked for supplemental information by the Prosecution, we could have done something. Now, the fact that Ms. Bilic is a civil servant does not mean she's biased. Of course not. There are Serb generals who have testified here for the Defence or for Prosecution. Belonging to the control of a command structure does not mean that they are biased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's time to finish for today, time to wrap it up for today. I think you have about 30 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have my notes here. They are not meant for distribution, either to the Trial Chamber or the Prosecution. Those are my notes, created by six years of preparation for my Defence, and created in preparation for Ivan Grujic, one of the announced witnesses. I can use some of them to cross-examine Ms. Bilic. But in order for me to get you documents, I should have had the opportunity to contact my associates, because my associates cannot give me, in one go, all the documents for all the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put an end to this right now. It's time to stop, and I have another trial starting in less than an hour. I believe that we can continue debating this tomorrow. We are fully aware of the question. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Again, it needs to be clearly indicated on the record there is nothing stopping the accused from having contact with his associates or receiving any documents from his associates, and this is simply non-factual information that the accused insists upon saying for the benefit of the public. It's not true, and we strenuously object to his untruthful statements in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the transcript now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. President. When I am able to eavesdrop and supervise the messages received by the Prosecution by fax, then I will allow them to eavesdrop my conversations and supervise the messages I receive by fax. Until that time, no way. Until that time, I will rather have no contacts and receive no documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness, you will come back tomorrow at 8.30, 8.30 a.m., but rest assured Mr. Seselj only has 30 minutes left. Of course, with objections and some procedural issues, you might have to stay for about an hour, but rest assured your testimony will end tomorrow. So please be here tomorrow at 8.30 a.m. Since then, of course, you're a witness of justice, you're not supposed to contact the OTP. Thank you. We will adjourn now until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 19th day of November, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.18 p.m.,
